title.en: Mass normalization, boundary parameters and count overflow

summary: Verify that a discrete mass function sums to one, handles boundary probabilities exactly and computes coefficients without overflow.
objective: Masses are nonnegative and sum to one within a stated tolerance, and boundary parameters produce a clean point mass.
applies_when: A scene shows exact probabilities for a discrete distribution.
Parameters can reach their boundary values.
Sampled outcomes are shown next to the exact distribution.
intent_signals: the bars do not add to one
what happens when p is zero
example_prompts: Check the exact binomial masses in this trial lattice scene.

principles: A probability mass function is a distribution before it is a chart: masses are nonnegative and sum to one over the support, and that identity is checked numerically rather than assumed.

Boundary parameter values are exact special cases where the distribution collapses to a single point, so expressions involving zero raised to the power zero need explicit handling, and the supported ranges of trial count and probability are declared rather than left open.
Observed frequencies and exact probabilities are different quantities and must never be drawn so that the sample appears to define the model.
implementation: Declare the supported trial-count and probability ranges, then compute the mass vector over the full support for those parameters, sum it, and record the deviation from one.
Evaluate both boundary probabilities and confirm that all mass sits at the corresponding outcome with no not-a-number entries.

Compute the masses with a method that stays in range across the declared support, such as a recurrence on the probabilities themselves or an evaluation in logarithms; a multiplicative binomial-coefficient recurrence still overflows for large counts, so name the regime the chosen method supports and cross-check a few entries against a direct computation at small counts.
Keep the empirical side separate: fix the seed, record the completed sample count, and compare frequencies with the exact masses without overwriting either.
observable_checks: The mass vector sums over the full support to one within a tolerance that scales with the number of terms; for a few dozen terms in double precision a deviation above about 1e-12 indicates a formula error rather than accumulation, and the tolerance is restated for larger supports.

Every mass is nonnegative and finite, each boundary parameter produces a single point mass with no not-a-number entries, and parameters outside the declared range are reported as unsupported rather than evaluated.
Empirical counts sum to the number of completed samples and stay distinguishable from the exact masses in both the display and the data.

known_limits: Checks the distribution arithmetic and its boundary cases; it does not establish that the modelled experiment satisfies the distribution assumptions.
Authored verification guidance; no computation or render was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: A binomial variable counts successes in a fixed number of independent trials with two outcomes and a constant success probability, and its probability uses the binomial coefficient times the success probability raised to the number of successes times the failure probability raised to the remaining trials.
claims.scope: Experiments satisfying the stated binomial conditions; trial count and probability are declared inputs.

source_refs.locator: 4.3, characteristics of a binomial experiment and the probability formula
